evals.name: orders-collection
evals.prompt: I'm building a Go API with anansi and need to add an `Orders` collection to my project. An order has: an order number (string, unique, required), a customer email (string, required), a total amount (number, required), and a status that can only be 'pending', 'shipped', or 'cancelled' (required). Write the schema file, tell me the exact codegen command to run, and show me Go code to: create an order, find an order by id, and query for all shipped orders over $100. Assume the standard anansi setup with anansi.Playground like my other collections.
evals.expected_output: A valid Orders schema JSON (fields keyed by UUIDv7, status as an enum with the three values, required/unique flags correct), the `anansi codegen golang` command, and Go code using the generated collection (Init/Model accessor, Create, FindByID, and a query with Where('total').Gt(100) and Where('status').Eq('shipped')) wired through anansi.Playground.

assertions.name: schema-has-orders-name-version-fields
assertions.description: Schema JSON declares name 'Orders', a version, and a fields map.

assertions.name: field-keys-match-field-names
assertions.description: Field map keys match their field 'name' (authoring convention — no hand-invented UUIDs); a real UUIDv7 coming from a normalize/migrate step is also acceptable.

assertions.name: order-number-unique-required
assertions.description: order_number field is marked unique and required.

assertions.name: status-is-enum-with-values
assertions.description: status field is an enum with values pending, shipped, cancelled.

assertions.name: total-is-number-required
assertions.description: total field has type number and required true.

assertions.name: codegen-command-present
assertions.description: Output mentions running `anansi codegen golang`.

assertions.name: uses-playground-and-model-accessor
assertions.description: Code wires persistence with anansi.Playground and initializes/fetches the Orders model (InitOrdersModel / OrdersModel / equivalent).

assertions.name: query-filters-shipped-over-100
assertions.description: Read query filters status='shipped' and total>100 using the query DSL.

evals.name: users-projections
evals.prompt: Add a `User` model to my anansi project. Users have: username (unique, required), email (required), a role that is one of 'admin', 'member', 'guest' (required), and an optional bio. I want three projections: `UserSummary` (just username and email), `UserCreate` (username, email, role, bio — with role required and bio optional), and `UserUpdate` (only bio, optional). Write the schema including the projections, show me the generated Go structs (especially the role enum and how optional bio maps to Go types), and show Go code using the projections to create a user, read user summaries, and update a bio.
evals.expected_output: A User schema JSON with metadata.projections (UserSummary/UserCreate/UserUpdate) using include/required/optional correctly, role as an enum, and generated Go showing role as a typed enum and bio as a pointer type (*string); Go code using ReadAs[*UserSummary], CreateFrom[*UserCreate], and UpdateFrom[*UserUpdate].

assertions.name: schema-has-three-projections
assertions.description: metadata.projections declares UserSummary, UserCreate, UserUpdate.

assertions.name: usersummary-includes-username-email
assertions.description: UserSummary projection includes exactly username and email.

assertions.name: usercreate-includes-role-and-bio
assertions.description: UserCreate projection includes username, email, role, bio.

assertions.name: userupdate-bio-only
assertions.description: UserUpdate projection restricts to bio only.

assertions.name: role-is-enum
assertions.description: role field is declared as an enum with admin/member/guest values.

assertions.name: bio-maps-to-pointer-type
assertions.description: Optional bio maps to a pointer Go type (*string) in generated structs.

assertions.name: uses-shape-methods
assertions.description: Code uses ReadAs, CreateFrom, and UpdateFrom with the projection types.

evals.name: query-migration
evals.prompt: I have `Customers` and `Orders` collections in my anansi project. Show me: (1) how to query all orders for a specific customer, joined with their customer record, sorted newest-first, limited to 20; (2) how to query orders where total > 500 OR status == 'pending' using the query DSL; (3) I just added a `shipping_address` field to the Orders schema — what's the workflow to generate and apply a migration, and do I need to rerun codegen?
evals.expected_output: Go code with a join query (LeftJoin/InnerJoin + .On(query.QueryFilter{...}).End()), an OR filter group (WhereGroup/OrFilter), Sort descending + Limit(20), and a migration workflow answer using `anansi migrate generate` (and `anansi migrate squash`) plus rerunning codegen.

assertions.name: join-query-syntax
assertions.description: Join uses LeftJoin/InnerJoin with .On(query.QueryFilter{...}) and .End().

assertions.name: or-filter-group
assertions.description: OR condition uses WhereGroup(common.LogicalOr) or OrFilter.

assertions.name: filters-total-and-status
assertions.description: Query filters total>500 and status='pending'.

assertions.name: sort-descending-limit-20
assertions.description: Sort newest-first (Descending/OrderByDesc) with Limit(20).

assertions.name: migrate-dry-run-then-generate
assertions.description: Mentions the migration workflow: `anansi migrate generate --dry-run` to preview, then `anansi migrate generate` to produce the migration.

assertions.name: rerun-codegen-after-schema-change
assertions.description: States codegen (`anansi codegen golang`) must be rerun after the schema change.
